agent: Claude Code (CLAUDE.md, this repository) — WP-03a verification: item (ii) AttemptRecord.inputs always {}
summary_for_principal:
This closes part of another checklist item from a past session.

Every record the system keeps of a single step in a process — what tool ran, what it produced, whether it passed its checks — was always saying "no inputs recorded" even when real inputs were used. That makes the audit trail less useful than it should be: someone reviewing a run later can't see what a step was actually given to work with.

Fixed for the most common case: any step the engine runs directly now records its real inputs. One case remains unfixed on purpose — a step that hands off to an external tool or reviewer and reports back later needs a bigger design decision first (recomputing the inputs at that later point risks the exact kind of subtle bug this session already found and fixed four times elsewhere in this code). I've written up exactly why and left it for a future pass rather than guess at a fix.

Full test suite: 364 passed, 1 new.

Numbered actions:
1. Nothing needs deciding right now.
2. Four checklist items remain — continuing through them next unless you'd rather reprioritize.

decisions.headline: D29 — AttemptRecord.inputs carries real resolved inputs for every attempt _record_step_result builds; report()-completed hand-off attempts and ROUTE/skip()/GATE-decider attempts remain {}, a verified, deliberately unfixed gap.
decisions.problem: Every one of the 8 AttemptRecord construction sites in engine/run.py passed inputs={} unconditionally, though spec §12.2 requires 'inputs used' to be recorded on every attempt.
options_rejected: Recompute resolved inputs inside report() the same way: rejected — report() does not build the full run_state (accumulated state from prior attempts) that node.in_ mappings commonly reference; reconstructing it needs a partial replay of _drive_scope's own walk, the exact mechanism class that produced D20/D21/D22/D23, all real bugs found and fixed earlier this session.

Have the caller round-trip resolved_inputs (already handed to it via NextAnswer.resolved_inputs at hand-off time) through a new report() parameter: rejected for this pass — widens report()'s public signature (every existing caller and test would need updating) for a value the engine would only be trusting, not verifying, a bigger surface change than this pass's narrow scope.

lessons.maxim: When an earlier investigation summary suggests a fix mechanism ('via the claim', 'via the caller'), verify it against the actual code before committing to it — the suggestion may be based on an incomplete read (here, claims only exist for MUTATION/SIDE_EFFECT Tools, not the general case) and the real, correct fix may be simpler or differently-shaped than what was proposed.
lessons.incident: The earlier investigation suggested persisting resolved inputs 'via the claim, since that's the only durable link between dispatch-time and report-time' — but claims are scoped to MUTATION/SIDE_EFFECT Tools only, so this wouldn't have covered the common QUERY-effect case at all. Reading the actual call graph found a materially different, correct, and much cheaper fix (the shared _record_step_result function already has everything it needs in scope).
lessons.destination: docs/spec/process-definition.md's own D29 entry documents the actual mechanism used, not the originally-suggested one.
lessons.proposed_check: Before implementing a fix based on an inherited investigation summary, re-verify its proposed mechanism against the actual current code rather than assuming the summary's own reasoning was complete.
